message.content:
Below is a concise overview of the key rights and protections you have as a tenant in Texas. (This is general information and not legal advice; for specific situations you may want to consult an attorney or a local tenant‑rights organization.) | Area | What the law says | Practical Tips | |------|-------------------|----------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlords may charge up to one month’s rent for a furnished unit and two months for an unfurnished unit.
• The deposit must be returned within 30 days after you move out, minus any lawful deductions (e.g., unpaid rent, damage beyond normal wear). | • Get a written receipt and keep a copy of the lease.
• Take photos of the unit before moving in and after moving out. | | **Habitability** | • Texas law requires landlords to maintain the premises in a safe, sanitary condition.
• Repairs for health and safety issues must be made promptly. | • Report problems in writing (email or letter) and keep copies.
• If the landlord fails to act, you may withhold rent or seek a repair‑and‑deduct remedy (though this is limited in Texas). | | **Rent Payment** | • Rent is due on the date specified in the lease.
• Late fees are allowed only if the lease states them and they are reasonable. | • Keep records of all payments (bank statements, receipts). | | **Lease Termination** | • Either party can terminate a month‑to‑month lease with 30 days’ written notice.
• For fixed‑term leases, the landlord must give notice if they intend to terminate early. | • Provide written notice (email or letter) and keep a copy. | | **Right to Privacy** | • Landlords must give reasonable notice (usually 24–48 hours) before entering the unit, except in emergencies. | • Keep a log of any entry notices you receive. | | **Discrimination** | • Under federal Fair Housing Act and Texas law, landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income. | • Report any discriminatory practices to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) or the Texas Commission on Human Rights. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlords must follow the Texas eviction procedure: serve a written notice (e.g., 3‑day notice for non‑payment), file a lawsuit, and obtain a court order. | • Respond promptly to notices; consider contacting a tenant‑rights group if you receive an eviction notice. | | **Repair and Deduct** | • Texas law allows tenants to pay for necessary repairs and deduct the cost from rent only in very limited circumstances (e.g., landlord fails to fix a major issue after notice). | • Document the repair costs and keep receipts. | | **Rent Control** | • Texas has no statewide rent‑control laws. | • Your rent is governed by the lease agreement and market rates. | | **Utilities** | • The lease should specify which utilities you are responsible for. | • Verify utility responsibilities before signing. | | **Subletting** | • Subletting is allowed only if the lease permits it or the landlord consents. | • Get written permission if required. | | **Landlord’s Right to Inspect** | • Landlords may inspect the unit for maintenance or to show it to prospective tenants, but must give notice. | • Keep a record of inspection notices. | | **Legal Assistance** | • Texas has several nonprofit organizations that offer free or low‑cost legal help to tenants (e.g., Texas Tenants Union, Texas Legal Services Center). | • Reach out early if you face disputes. | ### Quick Checklist for Tenants 1. **Read the Lease Carefully** – Pay attention to rent amount, due date, security deposit limits, pet policies, and notice requirements. 2. **Document Everything** – Photos, videos, written notices, and receipts help protect your rights. 3. **Know Your Notice Periods** – 30 days for month‑to‑month, 3 days for non‑payment, 24–48 hours for entry. 4. **Report Problems Promptly** – In writing, and keep copies. 5. **Seek Help Early** – Contact a tenant‑rights group or attorney if you receive an eviction notice or face discrimination. --- #### Resources - **Texas Attorney General – Consumer Protection Division**: [https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov/consumer-protection](https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov/consumer-protection) - **Texas Tenants Union**: [https://www.texastenantsunion.org/](https://www.texastenantsunion.org/) - **U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)**: [https://www.hud.gov/](https://www.hud.gov/) - **Texas Commission on Human Rights**: [https://www.tchh.texas.gov/](https://www.tchh.texas.gov/) If you have a specific situation (e.g., a dispute over a security deposit, a notice of eviction, or a maintenance issue), let me know and I can provide more tailored guidance.
